fix.notes: The `get_member`/`get_channel`/`get_role` lookups are synchronous cache reads (no network I/O), so they're safe to call without await. The fix also covers `/gbug` (Gatherling bug reports) which had the same raw-mention problem. No discovered-but-untouched issues.
fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

When users invoked `/bug` or `/gbug` and included Discord mentions (`<@user_id>`, `<@!user_id>`, `<#channel_id>`, `<@&role_id>`) in the title or body, those raw snowflake IDs were forwarded verbatim to the GitHub issue. The resulting issues contained unreadable text like `<@123456789>` instead of `@silasary`.

## What changed

Added a `normalize_mentions(text, guild)` helper in `discordbot/commands/bug.py` that uses a regex to find all Discord mention patterns and resolves each one via `guild.get_member` / `guild.get_channel` / `guild.get_role`, replacing with `@display_name`, `#channel-name`, or `@role-name`. Falls back to the bare numeric ID string if the guild lookup misses (e.g. DM context or unknown member). Applied to both `title` and `body` in both `/bug` and `/gbug` before the text is sent to `repo.create_issue`.

Also added `discordbot/commands/bug_test.py` with 10 unit tests covering user, user-with-bang, channel, role, unknown-member, unknown-channel, unknown-role, no-guild, multiple-mentions, and plain-text cases.

## Validation

- `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed (all checks)
- `uv run --frozen python dev.py unit` — 858 passed, 1 skipped (full suite, including the 10 new tests)

Fixes #5503
